title: Supported installers do not enforce externally anchored artifact authenticity
recommendation: Before any target write or launch, stage to a protected non-reparse location and verify an externally pinned publisher identity over the exact bytes; bind the whole setup/archive or every installed executable/evidence file, use stable file identity through execution, and never bootstrap first-install trust from a root carried only inside the candidate bundle.

title: The advertised two-signer release threshold has one CI failure domain
recommendation: Use separate protected signing jobs/environments or HSM/KMS identities that each see only one key and one exact pre-hashed statement; aggregate later, pin the public root outside the candidate bundle, and threshold-sign root rotation.

title: A consumed privileged capability is valid again after authority restart
recommendation: Persist an authenticated rollback-resistant consumed high-water and bind tokens to an unpredictable service/boot epoch, preferably anchored by a TPM counter or separately administered witness; add restart/replay tests before wiring an executor.

title: The production Sentinel CLI cannot give the monitored host verifier-only receipt authority
recommendation: Use an appliance-only Ed25519 response/state private key with a host-held pinned public verifier and a distinct client request keypair; reserve symmetric response mode for explicitly non-independent tests or migration.

title: Sentinel state signatures do not prevent snapshot rollback or cross-process forks
recommendation: Enforce an OS-level singleton, perform state CAS under an interprocess transaction lock, and anchor generation in a TPM NV counter, WORM log, or second independent witness; test two-process forks and old-snapshot restart.

title: TLS handshakes can block the Sentinel server accept loop before worker limits apply
recommendation: Accept raw sockets and perform short-timeout TLS handshakes inside a separately bounded worker or nonblocking loop; bound per-source/pre-auth connections, prefer mandatory mTLS, and test that a stalled ClientHello cannot block another client.

title: Trusted-time appraisal accepts a captured receipt without challenge or durable sequence continuity
recommendation: Require a current unpredictable challenge and persisted external sequence/time floor, compare against monotonic elapsed time, and label detached or unbound receipts historical rather than independently fresh.

title: Recovery assurance can report healthy for mixed revisions and future-dated evidence
recommendation: Reject excessive future timestamps and satisfy copy/domain/signer/restore/posture quorums inside one exact expected-revision archive/manifest cohort, with restore tests bound to the exact digest exercised.

title: The driver collector silently truncates at 256 and reports complete coverage
recommendation: Detect and report overflow or paginate every running driver under a global budget; bind evidence to kernel loaded-module identity and a stable file handle, add a >256 high-sort regression, and use signed hash policy while preserving unknown coverage.

title: Temporal and identity analytics promote EventBus integrity into producer provenance
recommendation: Admit analytic evidence through broker-assigned producer IDs and per-sensor sequence/loss records with a fixed producer-to-schema allowlist; treat EventBus HMAC as storage integrity only and downgrade unprovenanced inputs.

title: Several Cycle 24 foundations are not runtime enforcement yet
recommendation: Keep these controls labelled prototype or observe-only until protected dependency injection, key custody, transport, lifecycle, end-to-end fail-closed tests, and the required privileged enforcement adapters are deployed; surface unconfigured states prominently.
